body: Opposite the World Trade Centre is a fine shopping arcade with restaurants and smart shops including the Ministry of Crab restaurant and Odel’s and Barefoot shops. It is the oldest building in Colombo, built in 1669 a fine example of 17th century Dutch colonial architecture, with 4 sides around a central courtyard, open verandahs and thick walls. Floors had terracotta tiles floors, high beamed ceilings, and airy rooms with large windows, all designed to keep the wards cool. It was the first hospital to be built by the Dutch in Asia and served officers of the Dutch East India Company and Dutch sailors. However, when the British arrived in 1796, it ceased to be a hospital and served as a military barracks. Surprisingly perhaps, the building was still in existence, due largely to its solid construction, when Sri Lanka became independent in 1948. Since then the building has been used for various purposes. Before the 1980’s is was used by the Colombo Apothecaries. It was restored in 1984 by the architect Ashley de Vos. For more than a decade, it was Fort Police station. In 1996 it suffered severe damage from then LTTE attack on the World Trade Centre and It was abandoned, fenced off and largely forgotten. It was scheduled for demolition but in 2011, it was realized that this building could be saved, if it could be put to practical use. It was converted into a smart shopping arcade in 2011 whilst retaining the Dutch Architectural style. And what a fine job they have made of it.
title: 17th Century Dutch Architecture at its finest.

body: This was built as a hospital by the Dutch in 1681 to look after the health of officers and other staff serving under the Dutch East India Company. The hospital's close proximity to the harbor allowed it to serve Dutch seafarers. Over the years, this has been used for several different purposes (Colombo Fort Police station, Colombo apothecary, etc.). In 1996, It suffered heavy damage from the LTTE attack that followed the Central Bank bombing and in 2011, it was transformed into a shopping and dining precinct, preserving it's historic architecture. Today, this is a prominent venue facilitated with a number of bars, restaurants and shops, that also provides a great view of the city.

body: In the dutch era, it was a hospital. now it is a tourist hangout place with lots of restaurants, night clubs, live street music and shopping.
title: Famous tourist hang out place

body: I had a quick lunch in one of the restaurant and staff and service was good and place was ok. But the particular meal I ordered was not up to the good quality which is a lump price. Other than that it may be a good choice for a quick meal.
title: Nice place with variety may not be the best food

body: Nice view of the WTC, good for hanging out and grabbing some food with friends. Lively place with a variety of different restaurants and shops to visit.
title: Good for Chilling Out

body: This is a great place in Colombo to spend your evenings with friends and family.A very good choice of food outlets.During the day its good for shopping also.
title: EVENINGS

body: I love this place, Friday night will be more happening here and if u love to have beer with ur friends or buddies this is the place for that
title: Nice place

body: I love the fact that the shops are set in a single storey structure! where do you find malls like these anymore, house in a colonial building.It is a good stop for a meal or coffee. I love Barefoot and Odel for picking up local goods and Spa Ceylon for some pampering. There are restaurants for lunch/ dinner and would be a good idea to hang here. You see locals catching up from work and at night it is quite nice.
title: love this place

body: This is a small compact Colonial Dutch courtyard renovated a few years ago. A few interesting outlets such as Barefoot and Colombo Jewellery Stores, which have much larger and extensive shops elsewhere in the city, together with a number of restaurants. The recently renovated and salvaged buildings are worth seeing and make a good starting or ending point when exploring the Fort (by foot) which is nearby.
title: Colonial Dutch Building

body: Not a load of shops here as the area is quite small and there are some restaurants too. But what is here is good enough; Odell and Barefoot for example.
title: Good area uptown for shopping

body: The set-up is slightly confusing, but I will take some of the blame for that in that I am probably stoopid. Anyway, I ordered at the counter that had the dishes I wanted and paid at the cashier, but this seem to create all sorts of mayhem when I wanted an apple juice. As I said it was probably just me not understanding how this was supposed to work.I ordered a Caesar Salad (when will I learn?). It was not bad… it was just not a Caesar Salad. It was the closest I’ve come to the genuine article in SL, but there were no anchovies and what in the name of all that is holy was that thing masquerading as bacon? It definitely had never been inside a pig before, and I doubt it was even a known foodstuff. It sorta looked like bacon might look like, if you squinted your eyes and turned off the lights. It tasted of nothing at all and was largely, but not wholly, inedible. In short, don’t order the Caesar Salad.Food is reasonably priced; drinks are expensive.I will give Gills another go, as I like the concept. But I hope my next choice is more inspired.
title: Review of Gills Kitchen specifically

body: Must visit place to see Night Life of colombo.... Everything is quality and descent here .... You can spend 2-3 hrs easily ...
title: Night Life in Colombo

body: Lots of interesting things here including some good souvenir shops. We had a refreshing iced tea at Heladiv Tea Club with some very interesting flavours.
title: A great place to check out

body: Reasonably good shops including a smaller Odel and a couple of other souvenir shops. Worth a visit where you can obtain some good souvenirs
title: Reasonable shops

body: This is a must visit place if you’re in Colombo. The architecture is lovely. You can sit and enjoy coffee or if you have the money then you can eat at one of the many expensive restaurants and cafes here. The food is very good and you wouldn’t mind paying the extra. Once you’re done eating you can go shopping at the many shops available. These are mainly for tourists and you can find good gift items and mementos to take back.
title: Food, ambiance, shopping!

body: It is a calm and quiet place with great architecture.Friday nights are for crowd who likes loud music !!!
title: Good

body: A nice little oasis in bustling Colombo. Some shops but predominantly eating outlets. My daughter managed to find things to buy though. Worth looking at.
title: Nice and compact

body: Can walk around and spend some time food and other things are expensive Close to world trade center an other good 5 star hotels fort railway station bus stand and other shopping areas close to Galle face it's a god center
title: Just outing

body: Decent place to find a quiet food and drink.Prices and quality of the food is reasonable and varied enough to meet most requirements.
title: Nice place

body: The Dutch Hospital Shopping Precinct is quite interesting collection of old buildings, with a number of bars and restaurants, though these tend to be pricier than other places in Galle Fort. The walls and the views from them are much more interesting.
title: Worth a visit of passing

body: DHSP has been done up really well.A good mix.of history/heritage and modern place for dining.A must visit and happening place in Colombo.There are plenty options for food & drink.Few options for shopping, Odel LUV SL is a must visit/shop something.There are art stuff on display by local artists.
title: Good Hangout Place

body: This is a very cool spot in the midst of colombo city. A good range of shopping spots, restaurants and even saloons. You can spend as much time as you want here coz there's a large space for chilling as well.
title: Lot of activity!

body: We liked the Old Dutch Hospital building , however it's not really a shopping area per say , it's been taken over a lot by some Very High priced Restaurants and boutique Shops....
title: Impressive building , overpriced restaurants...

body: Don't be put off by the hospital name this is a beautiful old building with many interesting shops, restaurants and cafes - a nice slow pace and a bit of peace and quite away from busy and noisy Colombo city.
title: Old world charm

body: The old Dutch Hospital has been renovated and converted to a shopping precint and coffee shops. Beautiful old building, old architecture and design very well preserved, and a great spot to relax and have a coffee and browse through the many shops.
title: Great spot for shopping and coffee

body: The Dutch Hospital is right in the middle of the business district and offer quite a few shops with many options. It also accommodates few classy restaurants like the ministry of Crab. A must visit place of you are in the business district and want to so some quick shopping. The prices though seem to be on the higher side.
title: A Nice Shopping Complex

body: Visited the place with a vegetarian and an elderly. The Gills is towards the back end of the complex and not apparent as you walk in. You have to walk inside along the corridor near ODEL and then up few steps past an open seating area of a pub to reach the place.There was a descend choice of food. The spicy crab (although not very spicy) was my favourite.The place is a hybrid between a noisy food court and a restaurant. A friendly guy took our order and brought the food to us.The place looked nice and clean and is the only place for a family meal in the complex. Rest of the places in the complex are either pubs or very expensive restaurants like the Ministry of Crab.Good for catch up with friends.
title: Dinner at Gills Kitchen

body: Beautiful buildings with old charm. Great place for food and drink. Souvenir shops and a massage shop are here. Good spot for tourists. Love the ambience!
title: Great wee place to hang out

body: Whether tourist or local, Barefoot is a great destination for thoughtful, well-designed gifts, clothing and general lifestyle ware. While there's a tendency to be intimidated by the perception of high prices tailored to a tourist niche, a rummage around can elicit some great items - charming fabric mice for Rs. 700, ornaments Rs. 500 and above, cotton sarongs Rs. 1800. The Dutch Hospital location makes Barefoot more accessible to the local clientele constantly filtering in and out of the complex - and the selection here seems curated to include their more inexpensive items. If you're dropping by at O! Bar for a pint, a peep at their cheerful, artistic wares is unlikely to be a waste of time - and a Barefoot sarong is never an unwelcome gift
title: Mouthwatering Foods

body: One of the best places to visit during your stay in Colombo. 1# restaurant - Ministry Of Crabs!!! 👌
title: Fantastic Place!

body: Dutch hospital is one of the best place in colombo to visit in the evening to do some shooping and to booze with live music. Tap house by R&R the pub where u can sit outdoor and indoor as u prefer and live music. cheap snacks and beers.
title: hagouts#colombo

body: Lots of nice shops for fridge magnets or Sri Lankan shirts and bags. With a few good restaurants in the area. I visited the Ministry of Crab there. Well worth the visit.
title: Sri Lanka Holiday

body: A nice place to enjiy a little of upscale local artistic touch , nice souvenir shops , spas and restaurants , all hosted in a nice restored historic place Must go
title: Comprehensive cute little place

body: You can shopping...eat crabs...have a massage and spa... Recommend to everyone to go... Live music there also... Have a beer and listen to live music... Ps. Must bring some mosquito spray.
title: Must visit

body: It does seem bigger from the outside but there are enough options of things to do. The shopping precinct has an extention beyond the tap house area which has some newer dining / drinking establishments. The Odel has cool stuff but please check quality of souvenirs as its a touristy place and many people checkout stuff which create wear and tear on delicate items.
title: Small but neat place next to the twin towers

body: Lot of local made items available, Good restaurants available; very nice place to walk in the evening time
title: Good Food

body: Nice atmosphere in the evenings but it is much smaller than I thought it would be. I'm not sure what I was expecting but it was just tourist sitting around having expensive drinks outside a few restaraunt sand bars. We had one drink which was nice but then moved on.
title: Nice place but a bit dissapointing

body: The plaza was beautiful and well set up but smaller than expected. The shops are pricier than you'd find on the street but the atmosphere is pleasant, and you can reconnect with other foreigners. The restaurants are all high-end, try java cafe close by for something more casual.
title: Smaller than expected

body: At the heart of the commercial hub the Dutch Hospital Precinct is mainly active from 4.30 in the evening right up to early hours of the morning. Popular stores are Ministry of Crap, Dilmah Tea lounge, Odel and many other resturants, which attract many business and holidaying patrons from the World Trade Centre.Premium pricing and competes with all Park Street Mews patrons.
title: One of the few places in Colombo to have a vast court yard and surrounded by shopping brands and restaurants.

body: This is really old building(A hospital built by the dutch in the 1600s) that has been renovated and has some really good restaurants, bars, a few places for shopping(mainly clothes).My favourite restaurant here is the 'Colombo Fort Cafe', because the food is pretty good, and not too pricey. They have some reallly nice cocktails too.
title: Great ambie! A really Nice area to have a drink, and grab a bite anytime of the day.

body: The place has all the high end shops and resturants. Not a good place for a local to shop. Only look around. Highly overpriced items for locals. Good bathrooms, very clean.
title: Good for forigners

body: OK, nothing too crazy. Few shops and restaurants. I do not think you will be spending more than one hour looking around
title: It is OK

body: I have lived here for a few months now having arrived here from Australia where things are going from bad to worse ,feel so sorry for the Muslims they are been harassed every day. Anyway its refreshing to see even Muslims been treated as equal in a Buddhist country the visit to the Dutch Hospital Precinct was to find a place to eat as my grand son who plays with the under 19 cricket team was going back to Australia, we had a look at most of the menus' before we decided on the restaurant right opposite the entrance as the menu was western with some Sri Lankan dishes I had pork ribletts and a squid salad well it was better than I expected and the rest had pork ribs with vegetables and one had a pizza served hot on a plate all agreed that the food was excellent and the presentation would be about an 8 , the taste factor about 8.5 so cannot complain it was very pleasant ,do not go their for shopping as your first priority will not be a good idea ,do try the ministry of crab as we may not see these mud crabs for much longer and at what price one never knows ,great place for kids.
title: Worth the visit after hours

body: We had a few hours to kill before we had to get to the airport and we chose to come here. It was smaller then expected, but very charming and old world and worth it. It was pouring cats and dogs so we didn't get any idea of what surrounds the space but we ate and walked around and had some hot coffee and it was nice.
title: Pretty space

body: We dont really have any good malls, and stores are spreadout all over the city and a bit difficult to access. So the Dutch Hospital is useful in that regard that theres a few good stores to visit in one location, though the selection of items might not be as much as elsewhere. The prices are also relatively the same whether you go here or to any of the other outlets in the city.
title: One of the few shoppping areas in Colombo

body: This is a must Visit If you are in Colombo even a short stay could Visit this is in the center of the city very convenient lot of Shops Restaurants and a Happening place
title: Must Visit Just Amazing

body: My wife and I wandered around here last night. It has a wide variety of shops and restaurants nicely laid out in this old hospital building which has a lot of character. The restaurants and shops are not cheap as the target clientele is probably not low-end. As posted by some others, the Tuktuk drivers are a HUGE, HUGE nuisance. This seems endemic of Sri Lanka. The guides in tourist spots and tuktuk drivers persistently bothering tourists reduces a visitor's experience of this beautiful country.
title: Worth Visiting

body: If you need an escape from Colombo this is OK. The restaurants are decent and there are some nice souvenir shops. What really ruins it for me are the Tuktuk drivers. Of course they're everywhere in Sri Lanka and most are great and don't bother you much. Here however is where the greatest concentration of western tourists gather and thus is where the most annoying, persistant tuktuk drivers wait to jump all over them. Expect to get ripped off by any of them. Will not be returning.
title: Tourist trap.

body: There is a barefoot souvenir shop which sells really nice gifts.And that s about it. Restaurants here are expensive and serve small portions of mediocre westerner food. Some good desserts though.Would recommend to skip this place altogether.
title: Nothing special

body: Worth to visit this place. There are some souvenirs shop, pubs and cafe. You can also sit at the open space area
title: Just a walk and sit there

body: The Dutch Hospital is a trendy area with historical significance in the Colombo Fort area. I enjoyed the various food options and unique, boutique shops. I highly recommend visiting this spot during the evening when there are more people enjoying its ambiance.
title: Unique shopping and eating spot!

body: The Dutch hospital shopping center is centrally located and is easily accessible.Alot of trendy restaurant and boutique shops. Expensive. A visit would not last more than a couple of hours. Evening visit is recommended and weekends are crowded.
title: Great shopping destination

body: A nice place to hangout with friends. Friday & Saturday nights live band plays. Food and drink also available. Nothing much to do in day time other than shopping.
title: A hangout point

body: This was a hospital at some point of time now housing various restaurants and shops. The building itself is beautiful with its red tiles with the surrounding grounds. Some of the restaurants are really good here although a little pricy. Grab a cup if coffee, sit down at one of the benches and see the city pass by you.
title: Dutch architecture and some coffee

body: We were here for Ministry of Crab and while awaiting for our reservation decided to have tea in the court yard. The whole building has an airy, very colonial feel to it. There is a brief history of the building at the entrance and then it starts to make sense. I loved the stones as flooring and the wooden windows. We enjoyed our cup of tea and did a little souvenir shopping as well. The place is right smack in town and towered by hotel buildings. You cannot miss it, go at night to sit under the stars and have tea.
title: Old school architecture.

title: Great Experience

body: Nice place but over priced , variety of cousins ESPECIALLY sea food .. worth visiting. Nice outdoor settings.
title: Mr

body: Not so much to see there...There are several restaurants but few choices on shopping only Odel and Barefoot.
title: More on dining than shopping

body: Very nice place to visit with friends and relatives alike. Good ambiance, very good crowd reasonable price for drinks and snacks. Name is Dutch Hospital but a very nicely preserved old heritage site. Must visit once.

I suggest Majestic plaza and Liberty plaza for a better shopping experience.
title: Small

title: A great place to spend an evening

body: Good foodie place, but not much to do around, perhaps take selfies and sit out. Friday night there was a band playing outside tap house. During day not many around and restaurants were empty except ministry of crab.

body: Had gone there in the evening. Lots of restaurants to try ur food. The shopping experience wasn't that good

body: Kidna like this place, a few pubs, a few shops, a few restaurants.Mostly populated by the colombo rich kids and a few tourists its a fun place to hangout at but definitely not a must see
title: Average

body: With and old-world architecture, it's a nice place for food and drinks, especially in the evening. There are quite a few restaurants that serve good food and many different cuisines, and there's even a Burger King for the budget conscious. Being in the middle of the tourist area, beware of touts just rushing out to you from all corners (once you leave the premises) offering too-good-to-be-true deals.
title: Nice place for expats and tourists, beware of touts nearby!

body: This is a rather small place but I rather have quality than quantity. I did my Spa Ceylon shopping here and had some tea at Heladvin. Had dinner at Ministry of Crab.I like this!
title: Quality

body: We visited the Dutch Hospital one evening just for a look around and certainly weren't disappointed. As the name suggests it is the refurbished Dutch Hospital, a beautiful very old building. It is the oldest building in the Fort area of Colombo. It is now a spacious area consisting of two single storey courtyards, full of quaint souvenir shops, bars and cafes. There is a wide variety of eating places so my recommendation would be to wander around and choose one on the day! I believe you need to book well in advance for the crab one though. I have heard that there is live music every night Wednesday through to Sunday so it can get a bit noisy but with that there is a great atmosphere! If you want a quieter night, choose a Monday or Tuesday! It is a fantastic place just to sit in the shade with a refreshment and people watch!
title: A great wee spot.

body: It's an old Dutch hospital turned into a big courtyard with lot of restaurants and bars and few branded Sri Lankan shops. It is opposite world Trade Centre and close to Hilton therefore parking is always problem here. It is worth visiting for drinks and food rather than shopping.
title: Nice place for food and drinks !!

body: There are plenty of eating and drinking choices in this re-purposed colonial complex. A few craft and souvenir shops too.
title: A place for a treat

body: In this case the name does not say it all - not what I expected. This is an old Dutch single level hospital building turned into a courtyard surrounded mostly by eateries. It's cool and quiet and a very pleasant place to stop for a drink - a sangria for us - or a meal. There are a couple of nice souvenir shops, but 'shopping' isn't its claim to fame. Recommended for a pleasant break though.
title: Stop for a drink

body: Came here as this is one iconic place in Colombo and did not get disappointed. The variety of restaurants, shops and bars make it a nice place to stay and spend few hours
title: Nice spot!

body: This is a nice little centre with some nice places to grab a bite or eat or cook off with a drink. However I feel there could be more in there as it's a bit quiet.
title: Cute little shopping centre

body: Galle, in general, has great shopping options inside the Fort, especially for textiles & souvenirs.The Dutch Hospital has several lovely restaurants and bars serving a variety of cuisines at very reasonable prices.
title: Great shopping and dining area.

body: This area is steeped in history and has seen the benefit of some really nice restoration. Historically it had been built by the Dutch as a hospital and fell into disrepair when the Dutch moved out. It really looks quite good now.It's hardly a shopping precinct with only a couple of shops that sell souvenirs but it does have several restaurants situated around a courtyard that are open all day and evening. At the planning stage the architect forgot to draw outside lighting on his plans and as such both the courtyard area and the roadside sitting area are in darkness when night falls and sadly this makes the area look a little dim and dull.Many young local people meet up and sit in the dim light in the when night falls
title: Nice to Visit

body: Modern shops and restaurants in old setting. Makes for interesting mix of old and new. Enjoyable and pleasant place.
title: Mix of old and new!

body: It was located walking distance from our hotel so we decided to have a look at the premises. The setup is very nice. There are amazing restaurants in this shopping complex. There are souvenir shops selling beautiful souvenirs. Over all a great place to eat or shop for souvenirs.
title: Great Dining and Souvenir buy options

body: We visited in the evening and although busy it was never frenetic and all the restaurants and shops looked inviting. We ate well at Hapo's Colombo Fort Cafe and enjoyed happy hour drinks in the cobbled courtyard area. The crowd was mainly young but there were also families with children.
title: Oasis of calm in converted Old Dutch Hospital buildings

body: This dimly lit outdoor eating place is one of the best places in the heart of Colombo to enjoy quality time. There are variety of places to eat ranging in prices. It was not overcrowded the day we went but it might be specially in the weekend. I was tranquilized by the serenity and the blend of old and modern architecture. This is a truly amazing place to be and totally relax yourself!
title: Classic night out

body: This place is really amazing at night, have visited many times and would visit over and over again, looking at the night sky with the two tall scrapers at night is beautiful, it gives a feel of a foreign city at night.All dinning options are really great and nothing to complain about it.Would recommend anyone to visit here.
title: Wonderful place to be in the eve

body: There are many Dutch hospital shopping areas in Sri Lanka... this probably the most central in Colombo 7 (the good part of town) Has a good Burger King and a Dilmah Tea lounge which is great for Ceylon Tea. Some other luxury shops and restaurants complete the shopping centre which is good if you're visiting the memorial nearby... but not something you should really go out of your way for!
title: One of many Dutch hospital Shopping centres!

body: This old building has been given a new lease of life, inside there are great restaurants and a couple of shops. It is not a hive of activity but worth the visit.
title: Old history with a modern look

body: I love these hospital shopping precincts. They have one in all the main cities that I went to and I love them! The layout is nice and I feel like it's a good use of space. Definitely try out the Dilmah tea lounge! Good crepes and ice tea.
title: Lovely use of space

body: The old Dutch hospital is considered to be the oldest building in the Colombo fort area. Its now a heritage building and shopping and dinning precinct. Its a good chilling place with friends. There are many bars and restaurants amongst is the famous Ministry of crabs.
title: More restaurants than shops.

body: Loved the ambience, shopping not to forget the delicious CRAB from Ministry of crab. Lots of bars and great food outlets. Must visit in Colombo !!
title: Best Place !!

body: So many restaurants, all high quality, an ODEL outlet, spend an evening here. Nice open space in the centre to while away time with friends.Don't miss it if you are in Colombo. I ensure I come here each time I am in town.
title: Once isn't enough...

body: This is a great place to run in and pick up last minute items when you don't want to brave the crazy traffic and crowds at the flagship Odel store in ward place in particular. It's easy to get to, well known and has a wide variety of easily purchased items. The precinct itself is also home to the famous Ministry of Crab restaurant, a Spa Ceylon day spa and a small Barefoot store among other restaurants and little shops. The space is not large but not small either and is accessible and a good option for relaxing and shopping at the same time. There are plenty of tuk tuks surrounding the place and the cab companies are all familiar with its location.
title: Fast, easy access to some basics for tourist shopping with tasty food options

body: Nice setting for some tourist restaurants and 4 Shops. There is as well one bar with live music for the young and trendy.Nothing around. If you stay in one of the hotels close by a good Option. Prices are on european level
title: Overhyped

body: This is no shopping mall ! There was 2-4 shops, so NO shopping mall!! Restaurants only. And some spa.
title: No shopping!! Only Restaurants!

body: Went here with my sister. It is a very nice place to have lunch or dinner, the restaurants looked very good. Unfortunately we had already eaten and only had a beer here. You can also read and learn about the history of the place.It's a getaway place, hidden from the busy streets just outside.
title: A nice place to eat

body: A shopping complex together with restaurants. I noticed that most of the time youth prefer to hand over at this place. A good place to meet up with your friends , ofcause not under a cloudy sky.
title: Modern Posh and good experience for a personal space

body: I would like to comment how pleased I was with the service provided to me . During my recent trip I felt like I am at home hotel staff were excellent very hopeful specially the staff at the executive e floor and lounge.Very professional
title: business trip

body: The old hospital has been converted into a minor shopping mall with several bars and restaurants. Its Ok but nothing to write home about!
title: Nothing to write home about

body: What used to be a hospital has been restored into a lovely meeting/eating place. Once you enter into the courtyard, you are surrounded by a collection of restaurants and boutique shops. The centre of the courtyard has cement tables & chairs to sit and relax which also double as seating for some of the restaurants. If you do choose an outdoor seat, beware of the potential for rain as the courtyard is open air and not undercover. There are two courtyards that run parallel so you should have a wander around so you don't miss anything. Barefoot is down a side lane and ODEL is at one end of the first courtyard. There is also The Ministry of Crab, The Fort Cafe, The Tea centre, Ayurvedic Spa, the Taphouse, Burger King and many more.Outside of the hospital there are many tuk-tuks waiting to take you to your next destination. It's very close to The Kingsbury Hotel and the fabulous Colombo City Walks departs from there also. Definitely worth a visit if for nothing else than the history of the building and its restoration in the last decade.
title: A small oasis

body: We thoroughly enjoyed a lazy afternoon, strolling through the alleyways, remarking to one another on the heavy Dutch doors and window shutters with ancient hinges. The t Lounge was a nostalgic experience of luxurious teas in a charming setting. The local Steuart hotel is a capsule of Scottish culture and clans in its theme, although we didn't stay there... Just enjoying the sights and sounds. My mother's maiden name was on the wall, so very nostalgic! The Barefoot shop is fantastic, with lovely, thick hand-woven Sri Lankan cotton at a reasonable price per meter. Some of the spots are bit more expensive than other places in Sri Lanka, but many are the same price as elsewhere. A truly must do and see place... Something for every pocket.

title: A place with nice ambience to enjoy shopping & a cold tea in the shade under the low tiled roofs & attractive colonnades
body: The Old Dutch Hospital is considered to be the oldest building in the historic Colombo Fort area. It is believed to have existed since 1681, built as a hospital during the Dutch occupation of Sri Lanka, it has been used for several different purposes. The Dutch established the Colombo Hospital to look after the health of the officers and other staff serving under the Dutch East India Company. The building reflects seventeenth century Dutch colonial architecture. It was the Colombo Fort Police Station from the early 1980s to 1990s, prior to which it housed the Colombo Apothecaries. In 2011 it has been transformed into small new shopping complex, where the historic architecture has been preserved. It has few nice shops, few lovely tearoom - cafes and restaurants.It's a nice place with nice ambience to stop and enjoy shopping and a cold tea in the shade under the low tiled roofs and attractive colonnades.
